findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:486-499 overwrites a matching findings.json row with the original append-only ledger finding payload whenever recordId matches. finding_resolve only updates findings.json at handlers/finding.ts:821-843 and appends no ledger status mutation. findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:821-843 — finding_resolve still mutates only the findings.json compatibility mirror via readFindings/writeFindings and never appends a fenced ledger status-transition/successor record. The repository itself now demonstrates the lost update: commit e93c480257 resolves F-001, then commit 591642d288 resolves F-002 while reverting F-001 from resolved back to open; current finding_list confirms F-001 is open. This violates Story 3 objective that every Finding-system mutation be durable/exactly-once and lets concurrent closeouts resurrect a gate-consumed finding. Route resolve/dismiss status transitions through one append-only, idempotent fenced ledger transaction, derive the compatibility projection from the ledger, and add a concurrent two-finding resolve regression proving both resolutions survive and replay returns the original transition IDs.
findings.resolvedReason: finding_resolve, accepted-risk, and supersession mutations append signed fenced finding_lifecycle_transition records before projection; sequential lifecycle mutation and crash recovery selectors pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:131-155 — the new dependency gate releases a prerequisite solely when dependency.phase === DONE; it never proves the dependency branch is merged into local main/current baseline. packages/main/src/core/partial-done-recovery.ts:123-151 explicitly models the real failure state phase=DONE while story/<id> is not an ancestor of main, so phase alone is not the accepted DONE-and-merged contract. The smoke fixture compounds this by directly writeStory(... phase:DONE) and calling the dependency released, which cannot prove merged-state behavior. A partial-DONE dependency can therefore authorize dependent DEV before its APIs exist on main. Fail closed on both canonical DONE and a mechanical merge/ancestry (or equivalent signed merged-capability) proof, and mutate the merge fact independently in the dependency regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Dependency release requires the prerequisite Story to be canonically DONE on main and its story branch ancestry merged; lifecycle_dependency_gate passes for B-03b7 and B-e6d9.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:386-417,432-481 validates only the proposal top-level key set and shallow variant shape. It never requires FindingRef.recordId, the required dependencyBundle members, non-empty current witness receipts, or a truthful proposalSigner algorithm/keyId/trustRoot; receipt currentness rejects only the explicit boolean false, so an omitted result is accepted. findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:886-927,1107-1124,1131-1147,1232-1251 derives both the runtime signer and its fresh key status solely from the same invocation environment. A caller can generate a new keypair, set PROOF_OR_STOP_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_PRIVATE_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY, mint a receipt, and have that same unpersisted key treated as current; it can also omit the caller-controlled revoked-key env to remove revocation. finding_ledger_query additionally accepts caller-supplied trustedKeys. The production smoke itself generates a fresh key at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:808-838 and immediately persists a valid receipt, proving there is no independent repository trust/rotation registry. This makes signer freshness and revocation self-asserted rather than verifier-derived.
findings.resolvedReason: Runtime receipt trust resolves keys through the repository-owned independent runtime key registry instead of trusting same-process environment material; independent-process trust and tamper checks pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:994-1005,1131-1165 checks the canonical proper-lockfile mutex once, then runs build/execution under a different Story runtime mkdir lock. The canonical mutex is neither acquired nor rechecked at commit. Deterministic repro: pause the adapter inside its buildCommand after the initial check, acquire scripts/build-lock.mjs withBuildLock(root), resume while holding that canonical lock through CLI exit; finding_runtime_evidence_run exits 0 and persists a runtime_evidence_receipt. Thus a build that starts in the check-to-run window is accepted, so the build-in-progress refusal is not one atomic boundary with receipt production.
findings.resolvedReason: The canonical build mutex spans the complete build, execution, and publish window, removing the prior check-then-use gap; concurrent build/runtime smoke reports zero unsafe overlaps.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:561-652 makes the ledger/mirror append idempotent, but lines 677-705 unconditionally append reviewer_finding and recompute/write metrics after every replay, outside the ledger transaction and without the idempotency key. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts:59-66,83-103 performs realpath containment once, then reuses the unresolved logical dir for exists/read, openSync(temp), renameSync(destination), and directory fsync. findings.desc: F-011 remains semantically open: packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts:158-170 and 169-175 revalidate the runtime blob directory by pathname and then separately call openSync/renameSync/readFileSync by pathname; every validation descriptor is closed inside statIdentity, so no directory descriptor or lock spans validation through publication. A directory-to-symlink swap in the interval after assertRuntimeBlobDirectoryIdentity returns and before openSync or renameSync can therefore redirect creation/publication outside the project; the post-rename check can only report after the external write and cannot undo it. Preserve a directory capability/descriptor across open+publish (or provide an equivalent serialized primitive with no path re-resolution), and add a deterministic interleaving after validation/before pathname use proving outsideWrites=0.

findings.desc: F-004 lifecycle Authority is not closed: StoryStore.readFindings in packages/main/src/core/store.ts:484-549 consumes finding_lifecycle_transition rows after only core readLedger/validateEnvelope, but validateEnvelope in packages/main/src/core/finding-ledger.ts:289-340 verifies structural hashes/raw receipts and never requires or verifies the signed findingLedgerReceipt. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:572 — ledger-authoritative Finding can be shadowed by unsigned findings.json bytes when the mirror row reuses the signed Finding id but deletes or changes recordId. readFindings finds the id, skips replacement because recordId mismatches, and returns the forged terminal status; reproduction built current HEAD, created one signed open ledger Finding, rewrote only its compatibility mirror to status=resolved while deleting recordId, and observed {status:resolved,recordId:null,ledgerRows:1}. Verified by finding-ledger-runtime-smoke case finding.lifecycle_mirror_shadow_refused: PASS missing=open wrong=open legacyOnly=preserved (mirror rewritten to status=resolved with recordId deleted or altered still reads back open).

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:206 — idempotent replay trusts persisted exactRequestDigest even though that field is neither covered by FindingLedgerReceipt signature nor recomputed from the signed record bundle. Reproduction on current build: append same-key payload {v:1}, mutate only receipts[0].exactRequestDigest to the canonical digest for {v:2}, then replay same-key {v:2}; appendFindingLedger returns success with the original receipt while persisted payload remains {v:1}. This violates the explicit conflicting-bytes fail-closed contract and lets ledger-file tampering relabel a different request as an accepted replay.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 5fbda23bf8 (fix(finding-ledger): bind replay and mirror authority): exactRequestDigest is now part of the signed FindingLedgerReceipt bundle (FINDING_LEDGER_RECEIPT_EXACT_REQUEST_KEYS) and replay admission recomputes the canonical digest of the incoming request and requires it to equal the signed value, so a persisted receipt whose exactRequestDigest was edited to the digest of a different payload no longer relabels that payload as an accepted replay. Verified by finding-ledger-runtime-smoke case ledger.idempotency_digest_relabel_refused: PASS replayV2=refused persistedVersion=1 signedBinding=true semanticRelabels=4 carrierRelabels=5 legacyReplay=refused.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/store.ts:108-114 and packages/main/src/core/finding-ledger.ts:270-322 — verified L4 lifecycle-authority blocker: StoryStore accepts a current-key signed FindingLedgerReceipt that omits exactRequestDigest as long as the unsigned persistence carrier has any 64-hex exactRequestDigest. Independent temp-project reproduction created a valid signed lifecycle resolution, removed exactRequestDigest from the nested signed receipt, re-signed the legacy-shaped receipt with the current registered key, and preserved the raw carrier field; verifyFindingLedgerReceipt returned true and readFindings projected the high Finding as resolved: {rawCarrierHasExactRequestDigest:true,signedCarrierHasExactRequestDigest:false,resignedReceiptVerifies:true,projectedStatus:"resolved"}. Thus the gate consumes a transition whose exact request digest is not signed, contradicting F-018 resolution and the exact signed/raw carrier boundary. Require exactRequestDigest on the signed lifecycle receipt and exact equality to the carrier (legacy receipt compatibility may remain query-only), plus a lifecycle projection mutation test proving signed-field omission stays open.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:1358-1375 — high integrity blocker: verifyRuntimeReceiptCarrier validates the nested signed receipt operation but never requires receipt.operation === carrier.operation and never recomputes or otherwise validates the outer carrier requestDigest against its persisted request. Require the runtime consumer to reject signed/raw operation mismatch and bind the raw requestDigest to the persisted request, with end-to-end regressions for both tamper cases.

findings.desc: Legacy Finding terminal transitions are not crash-recoverable. packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:169-202 durably appends a legacy_identity_binding and assigns finding.recordId only in the in-memory compatibility mirror; lines 263-287 then durably append the signed lifecycle transition before the caller rewrites findings.json. An isolated current-build StoryStore repro deliberately omitted the post-transition mirror write and returned {durableTransitionRows:1,mirrorRecordId:null,projectedStatus:"open"}.
